units.text: INT. ARCHIVE READING ROOM - DAY
A high-ceilinged room of old oak tables and green-shaded lamps.
Dust turns in the light from tall windows.
Shelves of cloth-bound volumes rise into shadow.
A clock above the door ticks like a patient animal.
Five people sit scattered through the room, none of them looking at each other.
At the center table, a woman in her fifties named IMOGEN HARCOURT turns pages of a parish register with a gloved finger.
She reads with her lips slightly parted, and each time she reaches the bottom of a page she touches the corner of her eye.
Across the room, her estranged husband THADDEUS HARCOURT, sixty, pretends to study a map at the window, though his eyes follow her reflection in the glass.
At the long table by the door, their daughter ROSALIE, twenty-six, builds a tower of index cards and knocks it down by accident, and builds it again.
Two tables over, the archivist OSWALD BRIGHT, forty, in sleeve garters and half-moon glasses, stamps slips with a dry rhythm.
And in the far corner sits a young man named CALLUM FINCH, twenty-eight, a stranger to the family, with a laptop he never opens.
Imogen reaches the bottom of another page.
She sighs, and the sound carries.
Thaddeus turns from the window.
He crosses the room, slowly, as if wading, and stops at her table.
She does not look up.
He draws out the chair opposite, and she lets him.
He sits.
He folds his hands on the table, then unfolds them.
She turns another page.
He watches her thumb smooth the margin.
When he finally speaks, it is quiet, and the archivist's stamp falters.
You found it, then.
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: I found a name.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: Which?
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: Not yours.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: He nods, as if this is the answer he expected and the one he dreaded.
Across the room, Rosalie has stopped building.
She watches her parents through the glass of the index-card tower, and Callum, at the corner table, finally opens his laptop and then closes it again.
Oswald sets down his stamp, takes off his glasses, and polishes them on his sleeve, a private courtesy.
Thaddeus, why did you come?
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: To see if you'd read it.
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: I'm reading it.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: And?
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: She turns the register around on the table so he can read.
He leans in.
His finger finds the line.
His mouth moves.
When he looks up, his eyes are wet.
That's my mother's hand.
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: Yes.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: She never said.
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: No.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: The clock ticks.
Rosalie rises, crosses to them, and stands behind her mother's chair with one hand on its back.
Imogen reaches up without turning and covers it with her own.
Callum, in the corner, slips his laptop into its bag and stands.
He leaves, quietly, the door sighing shut behind him.
Oswald resumes his stamping, softer than before.
